chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding

the slave who falsely accuses a free man, he said: He is flogged with a full hadd, except for one or two lashes. This report implies that he meant by 'false accusation' that which does not reach the level of qadhf (full legal accusation), for that does not obligate the complete hadd, but rather ta'zir is obligatory upon him. And that which reveals what we mentioned is that Muhammad ibn Muslim, the narrator of this hadith, has narrated the opposite of this, in agreement with the reports we presented earlier.

key_terms.تَعْزِير: Discretionary punishment determined by the judge
key_terms.حَدّ: Fixed legal punishment prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.قَذْف: Full legal accusation of adultery, carrying a specific hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a slave who falsely accuses a free man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *jam'* (reconciliation) to resolve the apparent contradiction in the chain of transmission, suggesting that the reduced lashes apply to a lesser form of false accusation (*qadhf* incomplete) rather than the full legal penalty. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of harmonizing seemingly conflicting narrations from the same transmitter by distinguishing between specific contexts or degrees of the offense. The ruling underscores the distinction between fixed hudud punishments and discretionary ta'zir in cases involving social status differences between slaves and free men.
